newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - March 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - March 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- People working at the stock exchange welcomed the appointment of Abdelghani Gamie as head of the board and the change in the structure of the board.

- The chairman of Southern Cairo Flour Mills, Rafik Shalabi, said the government had decided not to give up its majority stake in four partially privatised milling companies -- Southern Cairo Flour Mills, Central Egypt Flour Mills, North Cairo Flour Mills and Alexandria Flour Mills. An official source has earlier said the government would give up its majority stake, as it has done in some other milling companies.

- The marketing manager at Watany Bank of Egypt, Ezzeddin Abu el-Maati, said the board had agreed to propose increasing the bank's capital to 105 million pounds ($31 million) at an extraordinary shareholders meeting. It has not been decided how much will be raised through a free share issue to existing shareholders and how much by public subscription. The present capital is 82 million pounds. The bank made pre-tax profits of 58 million pounds in 1996, against 30.8 million in the previous year.

- Yahya Qutb, chairman of Egyptian Financial and Industrial, said a feasibility study is being prepared on a project to produce potassium sulphate at a cost of about $120 million. Within three years it could add 120 million pounds a year to the company's profits.

- Net after-tax profits at Telemisr/Arab Radio Transistor and Electronics Supplies increased in the first six months of the financial year (July-December 1996), to 6.14 million pounds, against 1.882 million in the same period of the previous year.
- An extraordinary shareholders meeting of Misr International Bank/MIBANK early last week agreed a five-for-one share split.

- Extracted Oils and Derivatives raised pre-tax profits despite a fall of revenues, to 15.001 million pounds in the seven months ending in January, against 11.8 million in the same period of the previous financial year.
- Egyptian Tora Portland Cement raised after-tax profits to 78.5 million pounds in the six months up to December, from 63.45 million in the same period of the previous year.

- Memphis Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries made net unaudited after-tax profits of 16.869 million pounds in the first seven months of the financial year (July-January), against 14.575 million in the same period of 1995/6.

- Nile Match and Prefabricated Houses made net unaudited pre-tax profits of 1.173 million pounds in the first six months of the financial year (July-December), a decline from 1.775 million in the same period of 1995/6.

- Shareholders of National Societe Generale Bank decided at last week's meeting to pay out a dividend of 20 pounds a share and distribute one free share for every five. The bank made after-tax profits of 56.98 million pounds in 1996, against 48.39 million in 1995.

- Hassan Abdullah, the head of treasury at Arab African International Bank, said the bank would stop accepting applications for its bonds on Tuesday. The offer of bonds worth 300 million pounds was covered last week.
